Setting up coordinates with each square having side length 1 (vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1)):

**Square I:** The shaded triangle has the bottom side as base, with apex at the intersection of the diagonal y = 1 − x and the line y = 2x (from corner to top midpoint). Intersection: 2x = 1 − x → x = 1/3, y = 2/3. Area = ½ · 1 · (2/3) = **1/3**.

**Square II:** The shaded triangle has the bottom side as base, with apex at the intersection of the diagonal y = 1 − x and the line y = x/2 (from corner to right midpoint). Intersection: x/2 = 1 − x → x = 2/3, y = 1/3. Area = ½ · 1 · (1/3) = **1/6**.

**Square III:** The shaded triangle has the left side as base, with apex at the intersection of y = 1 − 2x (top-left corner to bottom midpoint) and y = x/2 (bottom-left corner to right midpoint). Intersection: x/2 = 1 − 2x → x = 2/5, y = 1/5. Area = ½ · 1 · (2/5) = **1/5**.

**Comparison:** 1/6 < 1/5 < 1/3, so S_II < S_III < S_I.

\boxed{C}
